subject: Instrumenting per-path telemetry and cost attribution for Acme Ops
messages:
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example>
To: alex_martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.example>
Cc: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Instrumenting per-path telemetry and cost attribution for Acme Ops

Hi Alex —

Acme Ops just raised a request during their renewal call: they want a per-"path" (they mean per-endpoint/route) breakdown in the Console that ties token cost + tail latency + request SLO hits to identifiable customer flows. Their ask is twofold:

- Visibility: a per-route tile / drill that shows cost (token spend) and P95/P99 tail for the last 24h and 7d, with ability to filter by model and quantization profile.
- Diagnostic: when a given route exceeds a latency or cost threshold, they want a playbook link (Doc + the list of recent request IDs) and optional one-click export for the last 1,000 calls for debugging.

Acme needs this for an internal SLA review next Tuesday (2028-04-10). They attached an hourly sample (acme-sample-hourly.csv) and a short exceptions log (slo-exceptions-log.txt) that shows their traffic shape. See Jira SUP-4721 for the original ask — I've pasted the link below.

Questions for you:
1) What telemetry fields do we need to enable per-request to power the Console tile? (example: route_id, model_variant, token_count, latency_ms, quant_profile, tenant_id, request_id, fallback_used)
2) How feasible is building a per-route aggregation view without increasing ingestion costs dramatically?
3) What minimal data-retention window do we need to support the one-click 1k export?

We should sync with SRE (cc'd Dylan) and decide if this is a product-scope request (Console backlog) or a short-term instrumentation task for Acme's account. Can you take point on feasible telemetry schema and estimated effort?

Thanks,
Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop
Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference
From: alex_martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.example>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example>
Cc: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Instrumenting per-path telemetry and cost attribution for Acme Ops

Lauren —

Thanks, this is clear and sensible. Quick responses inline, then proposals:

On Tue, 3 Apr 2028 10:12:00 -0700, lauren_bishop@redwood.example wrote:
> 1) What telemetry fields do we need to enable per-request to power the Console tile?

We should capture at minimum: route_id, model_name, model_variant, tenant_id, request_id, total_input_tokens, total_output_tokens, total_token_cost (derived at ingest or calculated in query), latency_ms (end-to-end), server_latency_ms (runtime only), quant_profile, fallback_reason (nullable), and success_boolean. If we expect reranking/chain-of-calls, add parent_request_id and call_index.

Proposal A (short-term, low infra impact): emit per-request summary events (one-line JSON) to our existing telemetry pipeline, store for 7 days at full fidelity, and pre-aggregate into hourly per-route doc for 30 days. This keeps ingestion bounded and lets Console show 24h/7d with drill-to-1k using the hourly index + selective fetch.

Proposal B (long-term product): add a dedicated route-econ index (columnar store) that stores per-request rows for 90 days and supports fast group-bys. Higher cost but required if customers want arbitrary ad-hoc exports and adhoc slicing.

2) Feasibility: A is feasible within 2 sprints of infra work (telemetry schema + one consumer job). B is more like 6-8 sprints and infra budget for storage.

3) Minimal retention for the 1k export: 7 days at request-level will satisfy most debugging windows. If Acme needs 30 days we should push them to Proposal B.

Next steps:
- Dylan, can you validate ingestion cost ballpark for Proposal A (estimate bytes per event, expected QPS from Acme sample file)?
- Lauren, I'll draft an API surface for Console tile (filters + export button) and mock quick UX so we can show Acme during their review.

Alex

--
Alex Martinez
Senior Engineer, Observability
Redwood Inference
From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.example>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example>, alex_martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Instrumenting per-path telemetry and cost attribution for Acme Ops

Alex / Lauren —

Thanks for the summary. I pulled the attached acme-sample-hourly.csv and ran a quick QPS projection. A few operational notes: 

- Event size: with the suggested field set (route_id, model, variant, tokens_in/out, latency_ms, request_id, tenant_id, quant_profile, fallback), we estimate ~850 bytes/event compressed ~300 bytes.
- Acme peak QPS in sample: ~210 r/s sustained with spikes to 420 r/s for short bursts.
- Proposal A ingestion cost: approx 300 bytes * 420 r/s * 3600s = ~430 GB/day compressed. That's non-trivial but doable on short retention (7d) for a single customer. If multiple enterprise customers follow, this scales quickly.

Operational mitigations I recommend for Proposal A:
- Continuous sampler: keep full fidelity for error/fallback requests and sample normal-successful requests at e.g. 5-10% (configurable per-tenant).
- Pre-aggregation job: incremental hourly rollups that keep counts, p95/p99 and token-sum per (route, model_variant, quant_profile). This enables Console to show trends without scanning raw events for every view.
- Export path: for the 1k export button, fetch raw events from hot storage (7d TTL) and stream gzipped CSV. Limit export size to 1,000 records by default with option for owner-approved larger dumps (requires billing review).

Effort estimates:
- Telemetry schema + forwarder change: 3 engineers, 2 weeks (instrumentation + tests).
- Aggregation consumer + hourly index: 2 engineers, 2 weeks.
- Console tile + export UX: 2 engineers + 1 designer, 3 weeks.

I'll draft an SRE cost estimate doc and attach it to SUP-4721 today. If we want the quick win for Acme's review, I can turn on full-fidelity capture for their tenant for the next 10 days (flagged account) and enable sampler after that. That will let Lauren demo exact numbers without product-level rollout.

-Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Senior SRE, Observability
Redwood Inference
From: ops@acme.com <ops@acme.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example>, alex_martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.example>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 15:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Instrumenting per-path telemetry and cost attribution for Acme Ops

Hi team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. We attached the raw hourly CSV and the small exceptions log you mentioned (two files attached). We are happy to have Redwood enable full-fidelity capture for the account for 10 days so we can demo this in our SLA review next Tuesday.

A few clarifications from our side: 
- We rely heavily on the quant_profile dimension to explain cost variance — please preserve that field.
- For exports: CSV is ideal for our offline tooling. The 1k default cap is fine; we'll request larger dumps if needed.

We are available for a 30-minute run-through Thursday (2028-04-05) morning PT to see the UX mock and validate the metrics.

Thanks,
Jordi Marin
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Operations
